tool: audit-context-building (dossier A: keys at rest and in memory)
skill: trailofbits/skills plugins/audit-context-building (pinned); run as a subagent writing one record per function to review/context/functions/ (crypto__*, secrets__*, cli__CLI__Credential_Store__*, cli__CLI__Token_Store__*, cli__CLI__Debug_Log__*; 78 records)
run: 2026-10-11; the dossier names no vulnerabilities by design. Its `nothing found` assumptions are turned into claims below; where the sharp-edges pass (same day, same agent, before the dossier) already holds the claim, the record says so, which is the independent-confirmation datum for the case study
independently_confirmed_by_the_dossier: SE-001 (fingerprint joined into a path: 'only `:`→`_`; `/`, `..`, absolute escape keys_dir')
SE-002 (clone signing keys unencrypted, PKI-store keys encrypted)
SE-007 (signature over ciphertext only; `f` is the sender's claim)
SE-008 (_pbkdf2_cached residency; cleared by two lifecycle paths only)
ID-005 (debug log keeps the query string)
AC-L-001 (Safe_Str__Vault_Path rewrites the root; all four store classes hold their root that way)

findings.title: a truncated or emptied vaults.enc reads as an empty store, and the next `vault add` re-creates the store under whatever passphrase is supplied: a local writer (A6) silently resets the credential store, and a mistyped passphrase on an empty store becomes the store's passphrase
evidence: _load_all L48-57: missing or zero-length file → {} with no error; any other content is decrypted (wrong passphrase raises InvalidTag, which the CLI reports)
store L19-24: read-modify-write, no lock (concurrent adds lose entries)
the file is the user's own; the attacker is a same-user process or the user's typo
findings.impact: loss of stored vault keys (they are still in the vaults themselves), not disclosure

proposed.fix: treat an existing zero-length store as corrupt (refuse, name the backup path) and keep {} only for a missing file; a sentinel header in the plaintext so a new store is created only by an explicit `init`
proposed.test: unit: an emptied vaults.enc makes get/list/store raise, not reset

findings.title: resolve_remote swallows any exception from reading remotes.json (twice) and falls through to the next resolution step: a corrupt or unreadable remotes.json silently sends the command to a different server than the one the user configured
evidence: L84-87 and L98-99: `except Exception: pass` after Vault__Remote_Manager reads; then the legacy base_url file, then the process default
TM-F22 pinned the server per command in CLI__Main.run; the dossier could not see whether that pin runs before or after this fall-through (open question for the verify-group dossier)
resolve_tls_verify L46-47 has the same pattern (falls to True, the safe direction)

proposed.fix: a remotes.json that exists but cannot be read refuses the command, naming the file; only an absent file falls through
proposed.test: security: corrupt remotes.json → the command refuses; it never reaches the default server (hermetic guard would catch a connection)

findings.title: import_read_key does not check vault_id against VAULT_ID_PATTERN (parse_vault_key does): a read-only clone with a vault_id containing '/' or '..' derives file ids from it (harmless, HMAC) but also passes it to the API as a path segment
evidence: callers: Vault__Attach L52, Step__Clone__ReadOnly__Set_Keys L25, Vault__Sync__Base L313 (clone_mode.json), Vault__Diff L593; the vault_id reaches Vault__API url building (host group dossier to confirm the API's own check)

findings.title: three readers of clone_mode.json disagree: CLI__Token_Store.load_clone_mode returns {'mode': 'full'} on a corrupt file, Vault__Sync__Base._read_clone_mode raises Corrupt_Error, Vault__Diff returns None; the read key in it is unvalidated by the first
evidence: a corrupt clone_mode.json makes the history commands treat a read-only clone as a full clone (then find no vault key and fail), while sync refuses; inconsistent, not exploitable as found

proposed.fix: one reader (Vault__Sync__Base._read_clone_mode) used by all three

findings.title: a token passed on argv is persisted to .sg_vault/local/token on every use; an agent (A9) that passes --token once writes the bearer token to disk for every later command
findings.status: KNOWN (by design: the skill documents it; the file is 0600)

findings.title: every secret READER uses plain open() that follows links (load_token, load_vault_key, load_private_key_locally, _load_all, load_clone_mode, load_base_url); the writer replaces a link, the readers follow one
findings.status: VERIFY (low: the files sit in .sg_vault/local, which the user owns; a link planted there by A6 points the clone at another file's bytes, which must still decrypt or parse)
evidence: dossier cross-function note (3); read_regular (O_NOFOLLOW) exists for working-copy reads and is not used here

proposed.fix: one private reader beside Vault__Secret_File.write: lstat, refuse a link, O_NOFOLLOW open; use it for the six readers

findings.title: dead or test-only code in the crypto layer: derive_structure_key, derive_file_key, generate_salt, generate_iv, store_private_key, load_private_key, Key_Manager.list_keys, Keyring.remove_contact, Credential_Store.resolve_vault_key
findings.status: CLEARED (redundant_code for the .security.json records; unreviewed code is unreviewed whether or not it runs)
evidence: dossier: no production caller for each; derive_structure_key is the structure-key split the website calls in-progress

findings.title: lookup_by_signing_fingerprint returns the first sorted contact whose signing fingerprint matches; two contacts with the same signing key (import twice under different labels, or a crafted bundle) make the label reported for a verified signature depend on sort order
evidence: L49-53; add_contact L10-21 does not check for an existing contact with the same signing fingerprint; the binding fingerprint↔PEM is checked at import (CLI__PKI L86-87) and trusted thereafter

proposed.fix: refuse a second contact with a signing fingerprint already present

findings.title: store_public_key writes bare/keys/<id> with plain open (umask) and non-atomically; key_id is not validated here (callers generate it with token_hex(8), no collision check)
findings.status: CLEARED (public keys encrypted under the read key; ids are generated, never user input; a 64-bit random id collision is the register's TM-R07 class)
